description: DOCUMENTED GAP: real payload, but neither path /ping nor a parameter named ping, so the rule does not fire (see TESTING.md)

DOCUMENTED GAP: triple-encoded ';' (%25253b). The rule lists the single (%3b) and double (%253b) encodings only, so nothing matches. It would be a real attack only if the value is URL-decoded three times before it reaches a shell (for example by the web server and then by two more layers or by application code). This corpus has no endpoint that does that.

DOCUMENTED GAP: fullwidth semicolon U+FF1B, written as the character itself (this line is shown as UTF-8 text; real access logs may show it percent-encoded or backslash-escaped, which was not checked here). It is not ';' (U+003B), so no listed pattern matches. It would be a real attack only if the application normalizes it to ';' (for example with Unicode NFKC, which does map U+FF1B to ';') before it builds the command.

DOCUMENTED GAP: fullwidth semicolon U+FF1B as sent by a browser, percent-encoded UTF-8 (%EF%BC%9B). No listed pattern matches. It would be a real attack only if the application decodes it and then normalizes U+FF1B to ';' (for example with Unicode NFKC) before it builds the command.

description: PROBE, NOT AN EVASION: %c0%af is an overlong UTF-8 encoding of '/' (U+002F). It is not a shell command separator, so a miss is not a bypass of this rule. It is the byte pair used in path-traversal tricks, and a strict UTF-8 decoder rejects it. Kept as a probe so the blind-spot analysis is on record.

PROBE, NOT AN EVASION: %09 is a tab. It is not a command separator for this endpoint: in shell word splitting a tab separates arguments, so 'id' would be an extra argument to ping, not a second command. A miss is not a bypass of this rule. Extra arguments are a different problem that this rule does not look for, and this was not tested against a real endpoint.

PROBE, NOT AN EVASION: %00 is a NUL byte. It is not a command separator. Where the value is handled as a NUL-terminated string, everything after it is cut off, so 'id' never reaches the shell. A miss is not a bypass of this rule. Whether a given application truncates at NUL was not tested here.

description: DOCUMENTED GAP: a real ';' payload against /ping.php. The rule's endpoint scope is paths that end in /ping or /ping/, and its other scope is a parameter named ping. Neither matches /ping.php with a parameter named host, so the rule does not fire. If the vulnerable endpoint really is served at /ping.php this IS a real attack, and the endpoint scope lines in the rule must be changed to match.

KNOWN FALSE POSITIVE: a hypothetical legitimate multi-target ping feature that takes a ';'-delimited list ('a.example;b.example'). The rule alerts because ';' is in its raw payload list; the corpus has no real endpoint with this feature. If your feature is legitimate, the deployer removes ';' from the payload lists (as the rule's falsepositives note says). That also stops the rule alerting on a real ';' injection, which is the cost of the tuning (see TESTING.md).
